html:
The St. James's Gate Brewery in Dublin is the home of Guinness. Arthur Guinness took a 9,000-year lease on the site in 1759.

From the 1770s Guinness brewed porter, a dark beer made with roasted barley, and its stout became the firm's main product. By the late 1800s it was the largest brewery in the world, exporting across the British Empire. The family gave money to Dublin for housing, parks and the restoration of St Patrick's Cathedral.

Guinness became a symbol of Ireland around the world, helped by the Irish diaspora. A Guinness brewer, William Gosset, invented the statistical t-test there. The company is now part of Diageo. Compare the Carlsberg brewery in Copenhagen.
